events.title: ALGOL 60 report published
events.summary: The ALGOL 60 report appeared in Communications of the ACM — the revised international algorithmic language used across Europe and academia.
events.about: ALGOL 60 added recursive procedures, call-by-name, and a precise formal definition — the model for how programming languages should be specified. It directly influenced Simula, Pascal, and C syntax (blocks, `begin`/`end`, compound statements). Most CS textbooks through the 1980s taught ALGOL-style pseudocode.

narrative.whyChosen: ALGOL 60 is the reference point for block-structured, formally defined programming languages.
narrative.whyImportant: Backus-Naur Form and the ALGOL 60 report set the standard for language specifications and compiler courses worldwide.
narrative.problemSolved: ALGOL 58 was a compromise draft; ALGOL 60 refined the design into a language compilers could implement consistently.
